data.name: Tomb Raider IV: The Last Revelation (1999)
data.detailed_description: According to Egyptian legend, Horus, son of the light, outwitted the evil God Set and imprisoned him in a secret tomb. Five thousand years later, Lara Croft discovers the lost tomb and unwittingly unleashes the evil God Set, fulfilling the ancient prophecy of his return to plunge mankind into darkness! In a race against time, Lara must use all her wit and skill to re-imprison Set and save the world from Armageddon. Pursued at every turn by her arch-rival, the unscrupulous archaeologist Werner Von Croy, Lara embarks on a journey of discovery across Egypt, where she must overcome the most ingenious puzzles and infernal traps ever devised, and face terrifying evil from beyond the grave... With more twists and turns than an Egyptian labyrinth, this is heart stopping action-adventure; a Tomb Raider that truly offers... The Last Revelation.

reviews.review:
i will not be recommending this. even though i thought it was super cool at first, thee problems i am running into are not worth it.

first, i will say, the game graphically has a little improvement, but the biggest is how lara is actually modeled. she no longer has sticks connected together, nor a diaper butt. instead she is actually modeled and blended most of the way and it is awesome to see. areas are super unique and interesting and it is really cool to see in game cutscenes with actual moving mouths. i have to say that this feels like the actual sequel to the first game with how much improvement there is.

there is actually a good amount of music and it sounds good, as well as a lot of ambience that isn't the same reused heartbeat for the last 3 games.

gameplay sees some more improvement here, with being able to have more agile movement, and skipping a bit of crawling, but you can't exit crawl spaces without turning all the way around which still hurts. lara moves into place, and i feel this allows you to pick things up while being less precise. but there are still some things that are so incredibly picky with where you stand, you won't know you are doing it wrong until you are in the pixel perfect spot.

there are some new types of enemies, different flying kinds as well as undead which can't be killed by normal means. so it helps spice up fights and make you think about what you want or are going to do.

some of my biggest complaints are, either me being dumb, the game not telling you of a new mechanic, or possibly what i ragequit this game at, a puzzle that i cant' tell if i softlocked myself on by doing what the developers wanted.

ther is one section early in the game where you need tto fish a key out, and 3 did this same shit. you go through using an item and she throws it on the ground so i didn't know this until 20 minutes of running around.

second is me needing to look up a guide multiple times to figure out there is a door i could pry open, but i never knew because i wasn't standing in the right spot to interact with it. as well as every game before this opening hatches by interacting with a button or lever somewhere. turns out, in the great library, all you have to do is walk up to it and interact with it. call me stupid if i was supposed to just know that i could use a hatch when  never could in any previous game, nor earlier n this one.

the last thing that is the final straw for me is this lightning puzzle in the bazaar level. you have 3 blocks you must push around a T patterned area. in order to do this, i assume i need to push on of them out inot the finish area, while juggling the other two into place so that, when i pull the first block  back out, i can swap it for the final piece to finish the puzzle. unfortunately, i softlocked myself there because it is random lightning strikes and now i can no longer pull the piece out, and solve the puzzle how i assume the devs intended. looking up video guides, everyone literally ignores one of the blocks and just pushed the final piece into place. i just assumed that i had to have an empty space behind me to push things, because that was how you were required to push blocks in the previous 3 games.

so, 13 hours into my game, i can't progress, and i am not going to replay all that time to just get back to where i was. so, while i like this game. ruining so much of my time i wasted playing this has me saying that i would not recommend this game.
